title: Efficiently generate all unique 4-integer ratios within a range up to scaling
body: I want to generate all unique 4-integer combinations where each value is in a small range, for example 1–10, and two combinations are considered the same if one is a scaled version of the other. Example of equivalence: [CODE] I want to avoid naively checking every new combination against all previous ones (which grows exponentially). Are there any algorithms, data structures, or precomputed tables for efficiently generating all such unique relative combinations? For scale, for ranges of 1–1000 for all four variables: Total combinations: 1000⁴ = 1,000,000,000,000 (1 trillion) Naive pairwise comparison to check uniqueness: ~ (10¹² * 10¹²) / 2 = 5 × 10²³ comparisons Even at 1 microsecond per check, this would take 5 × 10²³ μs = 5 × 10¹⁷ seconds ≈ 15.8 million years. Clearly, naive checking is completely impractical, even with modern computers, which shows why a clever algorithm or data structure is necessary.
